name: Myoelectric Seizure Projector MSP-6 'Marionette'
description:
The MSP-6 projects a directed myoelectric interference field that hijacks the motor neuron signaling pathway between the brain and skeletal muscle. Rather than inducing pain or unconsciousness, the Marionette intercepts and overrides voluntary muscle control signals, replacing them with a looping pattern of contradictory activation commands. The result is that the target remains fully conscious and cognitively intact while their body ceases to obey them — muscles fire in cycling, uncoordinated patterns dictated by the weapon's signal rather than the target's nervous system. Subjects typically fall, convulse rhythmically, or freeze in a rigid isometric contraction depending on the signal pattern selected.

Ringo Corponation developed the MSP-6 under a contract for a private correctional facility operator seeking alternatives to chemical restraint. The three signal patterns available on the production model — Collapse, Freeze, and Puppet — were each refined through extensive testing that Ringo has declined to document publicly. The Puppet setting, which produces the unsettling rhythmic full-body convulsion that gives the weapon its street name, was reportedly developed for 'aversion compliance training' applications. The weapon found its way out of the correctional supply chain within 18 months of production beginning.

The MSP-6 is uniquely disturbing in that it leaves targets cognitively present throughout the experience — unlike unconsciousness-inducing weapons, subjects remember exactly what happened to their body. Psychological trauma rates among MSP-6 exposure victims are significantly higher than among victims of physically comparable weapons, a fact that is considered a feature by some users. Targets with motor cortex augmentations or neural signal amplifiers are at elevated risk of prolonged effect, as the weapon's field interacts with the amplified signal environment in unpredictable ways.
specifications:
effective range: 3–20 meters
field width: Single-target focus (narrow beam) or 2-meter cone (area mode)
power source: Ringo R-Pack Standard (15 sustained-fire seconds per pack)
weight: 3.4 kg
length: 64 cm
signal patterns: Three: Collapse / Freeze / Puppet
effect duration after release: 8–45 seconds residual motor disruption
augmentation interaction: Elevated risk with motor-cortex augments and neural amplifiers
cognitive effect: None — targets remain fully conscious throughout
tactical_use: Law enforcement and corporate security use the Collapse setting for non-lethal detention of fleeing subjects, the Freeze setting for crowd control in high-stakes environments, and the Puppet setting is officially not used by licensed operators despite being present on production units. Underground operators use the Puppet setting specifically for psychological impact — the experience of losing body control while remaining aware is reliably traumatizing and produces compliant subjects. The MSP-6 is also used in arena combat as a paid spectacle weapon in venues where the audience pays to watch the effect.
cultural_context: The Marionette name and its implications have made the MSP-6 a flashpoint in debates about the ethics of non-lethal weapons in GLMZ. Advocacy groups point out that 'non-lethal' does not mean 'non-harmful' — the psychological damage profile is significant and lasting. Ringo Corponation's correctional services contracts have been the subject of investigative reporting that consistently disappears before publication. Among street operators, carrying a Marionette signals a specific willingness to cause psychological harm, which puts it in a different moral category than most weapons even in underground culture.
known_users: Ringo Corponation private correctional facility staff
High-end corporate security units (Freeze setting, officially)
Psychological warfare specialists and interrogation contractors
story_hooks: A journalist investigating Ringo Corponation's correctional facilities disappears; the last thing she filed mentioned she'd obtained footage of MSP-6 Puppet setting use on detainees.
A character is hit with a Marionette and experiences the full conscious-but-paralyzed effect — they remember everything, and they want to find out who authorized its use.
An underground arena operator is running Marionette matches as premium entertainment and needs the party to either participate or make the whole operation disappear.
Someone has modified an MSP-6 to broadcast on a wide-area field rather than a beam — and they've used it once already in a crowded transit hub.
